design.concept: A triage desk for the daily 8am notices. On the left, the person's notices by reference date with a quiet period filter. On the right, the chosen notice opens with its two totals and the tasks that were due that day or already overdue. Below the notice sits the delivery record, which is secondary and read only when the person wants to trust that the notice arrived complete.
design.decisions: One view, so no scene host. This follows the inboxSplit template: list left, panel right, and selecting a row fills the panel without leaving the page. The latest completed notice is open on arrival, and its row is marked as selected so the panel is never an orphan. The contract has no unread flag, no action and no counts, so none are invented. The page has no primary action button and no 'mark all' control, because nothing in the contract supports them. The list uses the alternative vertical record list because a table is too wide for a narrow rail. Each row shows only identity (date, totals, delivery status). The period filter uses the dual-calendar alternative, which exposes a documented change event, and applies the filter as soon as a full range is committed. A quiet 'Clear period' link resets it. Paging is only a quiet 'Show more' link and never a form field. The totals are metric cards that display backend fields as they come. Delivery status uses the success, error and warning tokens as small badges, so alarm color is never put on the rows themselves. The delivery timeline uses the timeline molecule with one event for generation and one for finishing (only when a finish time exists), and shows the failure reason when there is one. Loading, empty, error and precondition-missing states are written out in words, with retry or back controls. Each heading appears once: the page title, 'received notices', the notice date, and 'delivery record'.
